prompt: The interior angles of a polygon add up to $1440^\circ$. How many sides does the polygon have?
hint: You know the angle sum and need the number of sides. Use the angle sum formula with $n$ as the unknown.

hints.text: You know the angle sum and need the number of sides. Use the angle sum formula with $n$ as the unknown.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Check the formula on a shape you know: a quadrilateral has $n = 4$, and $(4 - 2) \times 180 = 360^\circ$. ✓ Now run that same equation backwards, starting from $1440$.
Set $(n - 2) \times 180 = 1440$. Dividing both sides by $180$ gives $n - 2 = 8$, which leaves one more step.
Adding $2$ gives $n = 10$, so the polygon has $10$ sides.

explanation: The interior angle sum of a polygon with $n$ sides is $(n - 2) \times 180$, so set that equal to the given total: $(n - 2) \times 180 = 1440$.
Dividing both sides by $180$ undoes the multiplication and gives $n - 2 = 8$.
Adding $2$ to both sides gives $n = 10$, so the polygon has $10$ sides and is a decagon.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the triangles
steps: $1440 \div 180 = 8$, so the polygon slices into $8$ triangles from one corner.
A polygon always makes two fewer triangles than it has sides, so $8$ triangles means $10$ sides.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap answer is $8$ — you divide $1440 \div 180 = 8$, see a whole number, and stop. But $8$ is the number of TRIANGLES ($n - 2$), not the number of sides.
Write the formula with its parentheses before dividing: $(n - 2) \times 180 = 1440$ makes it obvious that dividing leaves $n - 2$ sitting there, still owed a $+2$.
